chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Umar from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'from' 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'an-naduh' (a type of vinegar or preserved food). He said: 'Cook the dates until two-thirds of them are gone and one-third remains, then they are combed (or strained).'

key_terms.النَّضُوح: A type of vinegar or preserved food made from dates

ai.seo_question: How is 'an-naduh' prepared according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific preparation method for *an-naduh*, a traditional date-based vinegar or syrup, by cooking dates until two-thirds evaporate before straining. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding food preservation and consumption, illustrating how everyday culinary practices were codified into legal rulings within Shia tradition. The process highlights the emphasis on purity and proper preparation in Shia dietary laws, linking physical transformation to ritual acceptability.
